subject: Operationalizing signals into runbooks & alert routing
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@finlogic.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Operationalizing signals into runbooks & alert routing

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To make the observability handoff efficient I put together a short kickoff agenda and a proposed sequencing so we can get dashboards, tracing hooks, and alert routing operational within the next 3 sprints. Can you confirm who from FinLogic will own the following items?

- Signal owners (source/service) — who can answer questions about event names and SLIs
- Escalation contacts for P1/P2 routing
- Access for our integration account (service principal + minimal IAM)

Kickoff agenda (30–45m):
1) Current state overview (you) — alert types, most frequent incidents
2) Signal mapping review (we walk through our draft)
3) Tracing hooks & SDK placement (dev/infra owners)
4) Runbook & playbook handoff (roles, paging rules)
5) Next steps & timeline (owners + dates)

Deliverables after kickoff:
- Signal map (CSV)
- Runbook draft (MD) with playbook for common errors and rollback steps
- Alert routing matrix (who gets paged at what hour/incident)

I attached our initial signal mapping template and a quick runbook scaffold to speed the review. If the proposed timeboxes work, can you do Thursday 3/17 11am PT?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
[hannah_schmitt@redwood.com]

Attachments: redwood-signal-map-v1.pdf (pdf), runbook-draft.md (markdown)

Hannah —

Thanks for the clear agenda. Thursday 3/17 11am PT works for our infra lead (Sara), and I'll loop in our on-call rotation contact (ops-team@finlogic.com). Quick answers to your questions:

- Signal owners: Service team leads listed in the sheet below (I attached our current alert routing workbook)
- Escalation contacts: For P1 it's the on-call page then Platform Eng on-call; P2 goes to service leads and SRE team pager
- Integration access: We'll provision a service account with read-only log/event access. I'll request that today (should be ready by 3/17)

I'll attach the current alert workbook so you can pre-map any obvious overlaps. Also: two frequent incidents to prioritize in runbooks are (1) model timeout bursts during nightly batch jobs and (2) degraded KV cache hit rates after deploys.

See you Thursday.

—Tom
Director of Platform Engineering
FinLogic

Date: 2028-03-17T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operationalizing signals into runbooks & alert routing

Thanks Tom — looking forward to the call. I've pulled the workbook and pre-filled a few mappings against our recommended taxonomy so we can get straight to the tricky parts on the call (see column "Redwood taxonomy v1").

Pre-call notes (to save time):
- Prioritize the two incident classes Tom mentioned. For the model timeouts I recommend a 3-stage playbook: (1) scale policy trigger, (2) quick rollback N-1 canary, (3) cache flush + warm-up.
- For KV cache hitting issues: add a tracing tag for cache-miss-rate on hot keys and a synthetic check every 5m.
- Suggested alert severities: P1 = SLO breach > 5m or any deploy-caused 5xx spike; P2 = sustained error rate > 1% for 15m; P3 = single-service anomaly for 1 hour.

Deliverables I'll bring post-call: signal CSV, runbook draft with play steps, and a simplified alert-routing matrix for your on-call rotation. Diego — can you add estimated work items + story points so we can propose resource match?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior CS Ops | Redwood Inference

- Sprint 2: Tracing hooks + synthetic checks + dashboard templates (5 stories, 13 SP)
- Sprint 3: Runbooks, alert routing finalization, canary policies (4 stories, 8 SP)
